title: NYC Backstage Pass: Spotify x Design Meetup
hosts: Emily Shen, Sabria Islam, Mareike Carolin Keller, Design Meetup & Brandon Lee
summary:
Join us for an evening with three product designers from Spotify, each working on a different corner of the platform, for a conversation on building music products at scale.

When: Friday, August 7 · 5:00–7:00 PM
Where: Spotify NYC Office (address sent to confirmed guests closer to the event)

This panel brought together designers spanning mobile consumer, TV/desktop, and Spotify for Artists to talk through what it actually looks like to design for hundreds of millions of listeners, and how craft, collaboration, and career look different depending on where you sit inside one company.

Panelists

Davina Lennard-Alladice
Davina Lennard-Alladice is a Senior Product Design Manager at Spotify, where she leads design for In-Home Experiences across TV and Desktop platforms. With 25+ years in the industry, she's held design leadership roles at Meta, Audible, Discovery, and HBO, working across product, content, and platform experiences at every stop. She started her career designing magazines, and that print-era obsession with craft and detail followed her into digital. Davina is driven by the belief that great products come from empowered teams, and that experience quality is the thing competitors can't copy. When she's not thinking about cross-platform design strategy, she's hanging with her husband, two kids and dog, collecting sneakers, or making a case that listening to Beyoncé and Bad Bunny is the answer to most problems.

Mareike Carolin Keller
Mareike is a Product Designer at Spotify, where she's worked on the core consumer experience across Home, Browse, and social experiences, shaping how millions of users decide what to play next. Her work includes launching Spotify's first Author Pages, Spotify Reserved, designing systems that power upcoming release discovery, and more recently building experiences that combine human judgment and AI, such as an artwork system for Spotify's prompted playlists. Trained in experimental psychology at Columbia University after a brief stint as a flight attendant, she began her career in cognitive science and human-computer interaction research before moving into roles at Google (YouTube), Blizzard Entertainment, and various early-stage startups. Today, she is recognized across the industry for translating complex ideas about human decision-making into intuitive, culturally impactful digital experiences.

Kyla Windley
Kyla Windley is a Product Designer at Spotify, where she designs for Spotify for Artists and Music Expression. Her most recent launch was the Verified by Spotify badge. She built her design foundation as a Product Design major at Stanford as well as interning at companies such as Meta, Microsoft, and Nasdaq, working across healthcare, sports betting, and e-commerce experiences. In addition to Product Design, Kyla has a strong interest in learning about the music industry overall; she has experience as a Product Manager at a record label and artist management company, planning music festivals and concerts, and DJing many parties and events throughout her college years. During her free time, you can find Kyla knitting, at a concert, discussing the psychology of Love Island, or on a very long walk.

Who this is for
Designers/artists/creatives and students who care about their craft and want to meet other ambitious, thoughtful people.

Cursor is an AI-powered workspace where designers can collaborate with agents to explore, prototype, and refine product ideas. By describing intent in natural language, designers can move from concept to interactive experience faster, with agents helping translate design direction into real product changes.

Entrepreneurs First (EF) turns exceptional individuals into funded founders. Some might have an early idea, others may need a cofounder. What matters is their potential. We back these founders first, then give them a bridge to Silicon Valley. To date, their companies are worth > $16B.

Designers, builders, students, and anyone curious about the future of craft, AI, and building products. Come meet ambitious, thoughtful people shaping the next generation of design.

title: Figma Field Days: NYC Maker Night
hosts: Figma Team & Design Meetup
summary:
Join us for an evening of hands-on making at Index Space in NYC Chinatown.

We invited you to step away from the screen and make something with clay, paper, drawing tools, and more. You left with a creation that carries the energy you want to bring into the summer and a few new faces to bring it in with.

At Figma, we believe in making for the joy of it. This evening was built on that same spirit: a chance to slow down, follow your intuition, and create something that's entirely your own. No artistic experience or expertise needed.

Agenda

6:00 PM: Doors open
6:00 - 6:30 PM: Mocktails and snacks
6:30 PM: Welcome remarks
6:45 - 7:00 PM: Workshop introduction
7:00 PM: Open making session
8:00 - 8:45 PM: Gallery walk
8:45 PM: Closing remarks

Featured Artist

Photo by Danielle Hernandez

Ayaka Takao (she/they) is a New York based teaching artist and facilitator, born in Japan and raised in Honolulu, HI. With a primary interest in humanity, harmony, and love, Takao works across a diversity of mediums, employing of ceramics, painting, written word, and the World Wide Web.

Recently, she has been focused on an ongoing maintenance of a living, breathing website. Through her teaching practice, she tends to the human need of connection and self-actualization through haptic activity, leading with curiosity and sincerity. Takao tends to a polygonal, multi-disciplinary practice, mentoring others through education and embodiment, teaching collaboratively and rhizomatically.

Takao has taught ceramics and creative methodology in Honolulu, New York, Baltimore, and online, contributing as a guest critic and facilitator across the US. When not tending to Index Space and their personal admin, she enjoys slowing down in a grassy patch by a babbling brook.

title: Design Meetup x Reve Makeathon
hosts: Ilyssa Yan, Kyra Mo, Chi Quach & Reve
summary:
An afternoon of making, dreaming, and building, brought to you by Design Meetup and Reve at Reve’s Office in Palo Alto.

Design Meetup is a community for builders, designers, and creatives who believe the best way to learn is by doing. For this makeathon, we partnered with Reve, a new creative suite for visual work powered by in-house foundational models, known for its visual fidelity, artistic taste, and professional-grade editing interface. Together, we bridged the gap between imagining something and making it real.

What to Expect

2 prompts revealed the day of. A couple hours to build something, whether that’s a culture-defining campaign, a full product visual suite, or the imagery behind an interactive art-tech experience. Team up in groups of 2-4 with friends or through our team matching mingling. Project presentations and prizes to close out the night! Spots were limited. Open to all designers in the Bay area.

Prizes
1st place: $300 & 1 Year of Reve Pro

2nd place: $150 & 6 Months of Reve Pro

3rd place: $50 & 3 Months of Reve Pro

Every participant receives 1 month of Reve Pro

title: Design Meetup x Ramp NYC: Off The Record
hosts: Brandon Lee, Elizabeth Lin, Ilyssa Yan & Joanna Chen
summary:
Join us at Ramp for an evening of candid conversation and career mapping as we brought together five design leaders from across the industry. Whether you’re a student or an early-to-mid career designer, this event was designed to help you navigate the distinct paths of the design world—In-House, Agency, and Independent.

Through a series of lightning presentations and an open panel, we moved beyond the portfolio to unpack the personal resilience, hard truths, and identity shifts required to sustain a long-term creative career.

title: Design Meetup x Phia Design-a-thon
hosts: Ilyssa Yan, Brandon Lee, Joanna Chen & Sophia Kianni
summary:
Join us at Phia’s NYC HQ to build, think, and ship alongside other ambitious and talented designers.

🏆 Prizes

• $2,500 | $1,000 | $500
• Fast-track interviews for 1st place winner(s)!

👥 Format: Work solo or in randomly assigned pairs

📅 April 25–26

• 24 hours
• Phia's NYC HQ 🗽

What is Phia?

Phia is building the AI agent for commerce, translating consumer intent into better discovery for shoppers and measurable performance for brands.

In under a year, Phia has:

• Scaled to 1M+ users
• Partnered with 7,200+ brands
• Reached tens of millions in monthly GMV

Backed by Notable Capital, Khosla Ventures, Kleiner Perkins, and more, Phia recently raised a $35M Series A at a $185M valuation.

How it works

Stage 1 — Kickoff: Apply by 4/13 11:59PM ET. Standard app review through luma.

Stage 2 — Video interview: Submit a 1-2 minute video pitching an idea that you would want to build at the Phia Design-a-thon and how you would leverage your design background. (If you are selected, you can also change your idea. This is just to gauge your background and creativity.)You had one week to tackle a given prompt(4/14) due on 4/19 11:59PM ET. Finalists were selected and notified on 4/22.

Stage 3 — Design-a-thon: Selected participants built and presented to the Phia team 4/25, 4/26 at the Phia NYC HQ.

What we're looking for

• Strong craft & visual execution
• Sharp product thinking
• Original ideas
• Clear storytelling
• Realistic, high-impact solutions

Design-athon Rules

• One submission per team
• All work must be created during the event
• No edits after submission

title: Design Meetup x Clay NYC: Sharpen Your Design Toolkit
hosts: Ilyssa Yan, Brandon Lee, Joanna Chen, Johanna Pendley & Cate Waldram
summary:
Join us for a fun evening at Clay’s NYC office with lightning talks, and great conversation.

We kicked things off with food and drinks before jumping into a series of fast-paced lightning talks from designers building at the intersection of AI, visual arts, and business. After the talks, stick around to meet other thoughtful, ambitious designers during open networking.

Attendance was limited to keep the event intimate and conversational. Please ensure you’ve received a confirmation email to secure your spot.

Speakers

Elizabeth Lin — Design Programs @ Ramp
Personalized Operating Systems
What if software was built just for you? Elizabeth showed how she combines APIs and creative prompting to build small AI-powered tools and websites tailored to her own workflows.

Nikhil Singh — Product Designer @ Adobe
From Insight to Impact
How great product decisions actually get made: from core product design to product-led growth and 0→1 innovation.

Eli Miller — Designer @ Clay
What isn’t changing in design
AI is changing tools, but the fundamentals still matter. Eli talked about craft, communication, iteration, and presentation.

We were excited to partner with v0 and Cursor to provide exclusive credits for all attendees! These credits will help you bring your project to life.

title: Design Meetup x Framer NYC: The New Design Playbook
hosts: Brandon Lee, Ilyssa Yan, Joanna Chen & Sophia Cassidy
summary:
Join us for an evening with product designers from Notion, Spotify, and Netflix: the people building the tools and experiences many of us use every day.

Featuring:

• Jin Park, Product Designer @ Notion
• Mareike Keller, Product Designer @ Spotify
• Laura Sandoval, Product Designer @ Notion
• Samwoo Ee, Product Designer @ Netflix
• Neha Oblilisetty, Product Specialist @ Framer

We started the night with food and drinks, followed by an advanced Framer workshop/demo led by Neha, diving into modern prototyping and how designers are using tools like Framer in production.

Then, we moved into a candid panel discussion pulling back the curtain on how designers’ workflows are evolving: their personal career journeys, the shift from designers to builders, how they’re integrating AI into real product workflows, balancing craft with speed, and how they’re thinking about career growth in 2026.

Expect concrete examples, honest tradeoffs, and practical insights you can immediately apply to your own work.

After the panel, we opened up the room to a Q&A and informal networking.

Attendance was limited to invited guests to keep the experience focused and conversational. Please ensure you’ve received a confirmation email to secure your spot.
